analysis:
The only change visible in this batch is CHANGELOG.md (patch at lines 1-10, adding an 'Unreleased — DevNet' section). No executable source, installer script, or devnet-seed code was supplied, so this unit cannot establish whether any security behavior regressed. The new entries describe three things:
1. A non-production installer writes its own `[coordinator] url` into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml, and the production installer removes that line. Which coordinator a provider connects to is the TB-002 trust boundary, and the coordinator is trusted. The next pass should check the installer and CLI source for URL validation (https/wss scheme, no downgrade) and for preservation of other provider.toml settings. It should also confirm that the watchdog, LaunchAgent and update paths (T-043) read the same URL so they cannot be split across coordinators. A user running a dev-served installer is already executing code from that server, so this adds no new privilege. The entry also does not contradict the earlier 'loading a config never rewrites it' entry, because the rewrite happens in the installer and not at config load.
2. A new `coordinator/cmd/devnet-seed` tool fills an empty dev database with fake accounts, API keys, provider sessions and ledger entries, and refuses a database whose `users` table has rows. Relevant assets are A-007, A-008 and A-009. Dev is out of scope, but the next pass should check that the tool cannot be pointed at a production database. The 'refuses non-empty users' check is the only guard described.
3. The dev VM boot path now sets EIGENINFERENCE_IPAPI_KEY, a dev-environment secret. This is out of scope per the dev exclusion, but the secret must not be logged or committed.
No threat IDs are invalidated by this changelog text alone. Recommend verifying the actual installer, seed tool and dev boot script diffs, if they are in other batches, for the points above.
